column5: land and climate that shape a local product
column6: Voici le terroir dont ce vigneron est si fier.
column7: Here is the terroir this winemaker is so proud of.
column8: A typical word of French food and wine culture with no single English equivalent; it is often kept in French in English.

column6: Sa gourmandise le perdra : il ne résiste jamais à un dessert.
column7: His love of sweet things will be his downfall: he never resists a dessert.
column8: It describes a fondness for good food and is gentler and less negative than "gloutonnerie" (gluttony).

column6: L'élevage bovin reste très important dans l'ouest de la France.
column7: Cattle farming remains very important in western France.
column8: False friend: it has nothing to do with "elevation" and refers to raising animals.

column6: Le vignoble où nous travaillons s'étend sur vingt hectares.
column7: The vineyard where we work covers twenty hectares.
column8: It refers to the whole area of vines in a region, whereas "vigne" is the plant or a single plot.

column6: La pénurie de main-d'œuvre inquiète les producteurs agricoles.
column7: The labour shortage worries farm producers.
column8: It is used with "de" (pénurie de carburant) and is stronger than "manque" (lack).

column6: La famine a frappé la région après plusieurs années de guerre.
column7: Famine struck the region after several years of war.
column8: It is far stronger than "faim" (hunger) and describes widespread starvation.

column6: La gastronomie française est inscrite au patrimoine culturel de l'humanité.
column7: French gastronomy is listed as part of humanity's cultural heritage.
column8: It means the art of fine eating, while "cuisine" refers more simply to cooking.

column6: La malnutrition touche encore des millions d'enfants dans le monde.
column7: Malnutrition still affects millions of children worldwide.
column8: It is written as one word, as in English, and belongs to medical and humanitarian language.

column6: L'usage de ce pesticide est désormais interdit en Europe.
column7: The use of this pesticide is now banned in Europe.
column8: It is masculine; the more neutral official term is "produit phytosanitaire".

column6: Le blé est la céréale la plus cultivée dans la région.
column7: Wheat is the most widely grown cereal in the region.
column8: In the plural, "les céréales" also means breakfast cereal.

column6: Chaque convive a reçu un menu illustré par l'artiste.
column7: Each guest received a menu illustrated by the artist.
column8: It has the same form for both genders (un convive, une convive) and is somewhat formal.

column6: Ce mets raffiné est servi uniquement lors des grandes occasions.
column7: This refined dish is served only on special occasions.
column8: Singular and plural are identical, and it sounds more refined than "plat".

column6: Cette denrée périssable doit être consommée rapidement.
column7: This perishable foodstuff must be eaten quickly.
column8: It is mostly found in "denrées alimentaires" and belongs to commercial or official language.

column6: Elle offre une friandise à chaque enfant sage.
column7: She gives a small treat to every well-behaved child.
column8: It means a small sweet or delicacy and has nothing to do with "friend".

column6: Cet arôme de vanille rappelle les desserts de mon enfance.
column7: This vanilla aroma reminds me of the desserts of my childhood.
column8: It takes a circumflex and relates to food and drink, unlike "parfum" (perfume).

column6: L'obésité infantile est devenue un enjeu majeur de santé publique.
column7: Childhood obesity has become a major public health issue.
column8: It is a neutral medical term.

column6: Nous avons commandé le buffet chez un traiteur du quartier.
column7: We ordered the buffet from a local caterer.
column8: It also means the shop selling ready-made dishes to take away.

column6: Le merlot est un cépage très répandu dans le Bordelais.
column7: Merlot is a grape variety widely grown around Bordeaux.
column8: It names the variety of grape, not the wine itself.

column6: L'urbanisme de cette ville a été repensé après la guerre.
column7: This city's urban planning was rethought after the war.
column8: It covers both the discipline and the set of rules on land use.

column6: La banlieue où elle a grandi a beaucoup changé.
column7: The suburb where she grew up has changed a lot.
column8: In France it often carries social connotations that the neutral English "suburb" lacks.

column6: L'habitat collectif se développe dans les grandes villes.
column7: Collective housing is growing in big cities.
column8: In this sense it means how people are housed; it also has the ecological meaning of habitat.

column6: Le bailleur doit remettre un logement en bon état.
column7: The landlord must hand over a dwelling in good condition.
column8: It is the legal term; in everyday speech people say "propriétaire". The feminine is "bailleresse".

column6: La précarité de l'emploi touche surtout les jeunes.
column7: Job insecurity mainly affects young people.
column8: It describes unstable social or economic situations, as in "précarité énergétique".

column6: Chaque foyer a reçu une facture d'eau plus élevée.
column7: Every household received a higher water bill.
column8: It also means fireplace and hall of residence; in statistics it means a household as a unit.

column6: Le lotissement où nous habitons compte une trentaine de maisons.
column7: The housing estate where we live has about thirty houses.
column8: It is a planned area divided into plots of detached houses, typical of outlying districts.

column6: L'assureur a évalué le sinistre après l'incendie de la cave.
column7: The insurer assessed the loss after the fire in the cellar.
column8: As a noun it names an event covered by insurance; the adjective "sinistre" means ominous.

column6: Elle a utilisé son héritage pour acheter un petit appartement.
column7: She used her inheritance to buy a small flat.
column8: It also means a cultural legacy handed down from the past.

column5: settlement of a deceased person's estate
column6: La succession de leur père a été réglée en quelques mois.
column7: The settlement of their father's estate was completed in a few months.
column8: In law it is the procedure that sorts out a deceased person's property; it also means a series.

column6: Dans notre fratrie, je suis la cadette.
column7: Among my siblings, I am the youngest.
column8: English has no everyday single word for it; it names all children of a family as a group.

column6: Le mineur a été placé sous la tutelle de son oncle.
column7: The minor was placed under his uncle's guardianship.
column8: It also means oversight of a body by an authority.

column6: La vieillesse n'empêche pas de rester curieux et actif.
column7: Old age does not stop people from staying curious and active.
column8: It is neutral or slightly literary; "troisième âge" is the gentler expression.

column6: La solitude pèse sur de nombreuses personnes âgées en ville.
column7: Loneliness weighs on many elderly people in cities.
column8: It can be neutral (being alone) or negative; "isolement" is clearly negative.

column6: La cohabitation entre générations devient de plus en plus fréquente.
column7: Living together across generations is becoming more and more common.
column8: In French politics it also means a period when president and government come from opposing camps.

column6: La rénovation de l'immeuble a duré plus d'un an.
column7: The renovation of the building lasted more than a year.
column8: It covers repairs and upgrades of buildings, often with the word "rénover".

column6: La charpente de cette grange date de plusieurs siècles.
column7: The roof framework of this barn is several centuries old.
column8: It means the load-bearing structure, usually timber; figuratively it is the skeleton of a text.

column6: Laissez vos manteaux dans le vestibule avant d'entrer au salon.
column7: Leave your coats in the hall before going into the living room.
column8: More formal than "entrée", which is the everyday word.

column5: layout and fitting out of a space
column6: L'aménagement du salon a pris deux semaines.
column7: Fitting out the living room took two weeks.
column8: It is also used for land-use planning ("aménagement du territoire").

column6: L'expulsion de la famille a été reportée à l'hiver.
column7: The family's eviction was postponed until winter.
column8: It also means expulsion of a foreigner or a pupil.

column6: Plus d'un million d'habitants vivent dans cette agglomération.
column7: More than a million inhabitants live in this urban area.
column8: A statistical and administrative term covering a city and its neighbouring towns.

column6: L'inflation a réduit le pouvoir d'achat de nombreux ménages.
column7: Inflation has reduced the purchasing power of many households.
column8: It is almost always used in the singular; the opposite is "déflation".

column6: La banque a pris une hypothèque sur leur maison.
column7: The bank took a mortgage on their house.
column8: It is the security right on the property; the loan itself is called "prêt immobilier".

column6: La clause dont il conteste la validité figure à l'article cinq.
column7: The clause whose validity he disputes appears in article five.
column8: It belongs to contract law, as in "clause abusive" (unfair term).

column6: Le litige entre les deux sociétés est porté devant le tribunal.
column7: The dispute between the two companies has been brought before the court.
column8: A formal and often legal word; for a simple quarrel one says "dispute".

column6: Le client a subi un préjudice financier important.
column7: The customer suffered considerable financial harm.
column8: False friend: it does not mean a biased opinion, which is "préjugé".

column6: Il a reçu une indemnité de départ de six mois.
column7: He received a severance payment of six months.
column8: It is a payment made as compensation or allowance under law or contract.

column6: La cotisation annuelle au club a augmenté cette année.
column7: The annual club subscription has gone up this year.
column8: It also covers social-security contributions and is not a tax ("impôt").

column6: Le délai de rétractation est de quatorze jours.
column7: The withdrawal period is fourteen days.
column8: In consumer law the phrase is "droit de rétractation"; it also means retracting a statement.

column6: Le propriétaire a exigé une caution avant de signer le bail.
column7: The landlord demanded a guarantor before signing the lease.
column8: It names both the guarantee and the person who stands surety; a deposit is "dépôt de garantie".

column6: Le créancier a réclamé le remboursement de la somme avancée.
column7: The creditor demanded repayment of the sum advanced.
column8: The opposite is "débiteur"; the feminine is "créancière".

column6: Le bail prévoit un loyer révisable chaque année.
column7: The lease provides for rent that can be revised every year.
column8: The plural is irregular: "les baux".

column6: Il a versé un acompte pour réserver le canapé.
column7: He paid a deposit to reserve the sofa.
column8: It is part of the price paid in advance and is legally different from "arrhes".

column6: Cette annonce immobilière était une escroquerie bien organisée.
column7: This property advert was a well-organised swindle.
column8: It is the legal term for an offence; "arnaque" is the more familiar word.

column6: La contrefaçon de produits de luxe coûte cher aux marques.
column7: The counterfeiting of luxury goods costs brands dearly.
column8: It means both the offence and the fake item, and it takes a cedilla.

column6: Une pénalité de retard s'applique après quinze jours.
column7: A late-payment penalty applies after fifteen days.
column8: It is a sum due for breach of contract; in football French uses "penalty".

column6: Nous avons demandé un devis à trois entreprises différentes.
column7: We asked three different companies for a quote.
column8: The plural is identical to the singular and it has nothing to do with "device".

column6: La faillite de ce fournisseur a surpris tout le secteur.
column7: The supplier's bankruptcy surprised the whole sector.
column8: It is used for companies; figuratively it means a complete failure.

column6: Cette entreprise détient le monopole du marché local.
column7: This company holds the monopoly of the local market.
column8: It is often found in expressions such as "monopole d'État" (state monopoly).

column6: L'obsolescence programmée irrite de nombreux consommateurs.
column7: Planned obsolescence irritates many consumers.
column8: It is mostly found in the phrase "obsolescence programmée".

column6: Le consommateur dispose d'un recours devant le tribunal.
column7: The consumer has a legal remedy before the court.
column8: It is common in "avoir recours à" (to resort to); the final s is silent.

column6: Nous avons fait une escapade de deux jours en Normandie.
column7: We took a two-day getaway in Normandy.
column8: Refers to a short pleasure trip, often spontaneous, taken to escape routine.

column6: Nous avons installé le bivouac où le vent ne soufflait pas.
column7: We set up the bivouac where the wind was not blowing.
column8: A light open-air camp, often in the mountains, with no permanent facilities.

column6: Cette côte est une station de villégiature très prisée en été.
column7: This coast is a very popular holiday resort in summer.
column8: A formal word for a holiday stay or the place where one stays; the usual phrase is « lieu de villégiature ».

column6: Chaque année, il fait le pèlerinage jusqu'à Saint-Jacques-de-Compostelle.
column7: Every year he makes the pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela.
column8: A journey to a holy place; figuratively, a moving visit to a place that matters to someone.

column6: La traversée en ferry a été agitée à cause du vent.
column7: The ferry crossing was rough because of the wind.
column8: Refers to the trip from one shore to another, mostly by sea; also used figuratively (« traversée du désert »).

column6: Nous avons été touchés par l'hospitalité de nos hôtes.
column7: We were touched by our hosts' hospitality.
column8: Refers to the generous welcome of a guest; for the hotel industry the usual word is l'hôtellerie.

column6: L'hôtellerie de luxe attire une clientèle internationale.
column7: The luxury hotel industry attracts an international clientele.
column8: Refers to hotels as a business sector; the common phrase is « hôtellerie-restauration ».

column6: L'aérogare est desservie par une navette gratuite.
column7: The air terminal is served by a free shuttle.
column8: The building reserved for an airport's passengers; the English word terminal (masculine) is also very common.

column6: Le mandat du président dure cinq ans.
column7: The president's term lasts five years.
column8: Refers to the length of an elected office; in law it is also the authority to act on someone's behalf.

column6: Les deux parties ont accepté l'arbitrage d'un expert indépendant.
column7: Both parties accepted arbitration by an independent expert.
column8: Settling a dispute through a chosen third party; the word also covers a sports referee's decisions.

column6: Sa rémunération comprend un salaire fixe et une prime annuelle.
column7: His remuneration includes a fixed salary and an annual bonus.
column8: A more formal term than salaire; it covers every sum paid for work done.

column6: La rentabilité du projet reste encore à démontrer.
column7: The project's profitability still has to be demonstrated.
column8: The ability of an activity to produce a profit; the matching adjective is rentable.

column6: La prestation comprend l'installation et la formation du personnel.
column7: The service includes installation and staff training.
column8: Used in « prestation de service »; in the plural, prestations sociales are benefits paid by the State.

column6: La procédure de recrutement dure généralement trois mois.
column7: The recruitment procedure generally lasts three months.
column8: A series of steps to follow; in law it also means how a legal action proceeds.

column6: Il a déposé une plainte contre son ancien employeur.
column7: He filed a complaint against his former employer.
column8: One « dépose » or « porte » plainte with the police; the word can also mean a moan.

column6: La fusion des deux banques a été annoncée hier.
column7: The merger of the two banks was announced yesterday.
column8: Refers to two companies becoming one; in physics, the change from solid to liquid.

column6: Le patronat et les syndicats négocient une nouvelle convention.
column7: Employers and unions are negotiating a new agreement.
column8: All employers taken together, often set against the unions; one also says « les organisations patronales ».

column6: Le poète file la métaphore tout au long du texte.
column7: The poet extends the metaphor throughout the text.
column8: « Filer la métaphore » means to develop it further; not to be confused with a comparison, which uses comme.

column6: Son dernier essai analyse la crise de la démocratie.
column7: His latest essay analyses the crisis of democracy.
column8: A literary genre of reflective prose; the word also means an attempt, and in rugby a try scored.

column6: Le récit de son voyage se lit d'une traite.
column7: The account of his journey can be read in one go.
column8: A text or speech that tells real or imagined events; the final t is silent.

column6: L'intrigue du film est difficile à suivre.
column7: The plot of the film is hard to follow.
column8: Refers to the chain of events in a story; the word also means a secret scheme.

column6: Voici une intrigue dont le dénouement reste imprévisible.
column7: Here is a plot whose resolution remains unpredictable.
column8: The moment when the plot of a play or novel is resolved; by extension, the outcome of a situation.

column6: Le critique a fait l'éloge de cette mise en scène.
column7: The critic praised this staging.
column8: Used mostly in « faire l'éloge de »; an éloge funèbre is a speech honouring the dead.

column6: Ce roman est une satire féroce de la bureaucratie.
column7: This novel is a fierce satire of bureaucracy.
column8: A work or genre that criticises a society's faults through mockery.

column6: La censure a interdit la diffusion de ce documentaire.
column7: Censorship banned the broadcasting of this documentary.
column8: Control exercised by an authority over publications or shows; in politics, also a vote that topples a government.

column6: Cette idéologie a profondément marqué le siècle dernier.
column7: This ideology deeply marked the last century.
column8: A set of ideas guiding a group; the word often carries a negative nuance.

column6: Le scrutin aura lieu dimanche prochain dans toute la France.
column7: The vote will take place next Sunday across France.
column8: Refers to the act of voting or the electoral system; one says « un scrutin à deux tours ».

column6: Cette réforme des retraites a provoqué de vives protestations.
column7: This pension reform provoked strong protests.
column8: A deep change to an institution or law; the capitalised Réforme refers to the sixteenth-century religious movement.

column6: C'est une doctrine dont les effets restent très discutés.
column7: It is a doctrine whose effects remain much debated.
column8: A body of principles upheld by a school, religion or party; the tone is often serious or critical.

column6: Elle se trouve face à un dilemme moral difficile.
column7: She faces a difficult moral dilemma.
column8: A masculine noun; it means a choice between two equally unpleasant options.

column6: Il y a un paradoxe dans sa manière de vivre.
column7: There is a paradox in his way of living.
column8: A statement or situation that seems contradictory; one says « par paradoxe » to introduce a contrast.

column6: Ce préjugé tenace persiste malgré toutes les études.
column7: This stubborn prejudice persists despite all the studies.
column8: A ready-made opinion adopted without examination; not to be confused with préjudice, which means harm.

column6: Elle tient une chronique hebdomadaire dans un grand quotidien.
column7: She writes a weekly column in a major daily newspaper.
column8: A regular article by a journalist on a given subject; the word also means a historical account.

column6: L'éditorial du journal critique la politique du gouvernement.
column7: The newspaper's editorial criticises the government's policy.
column8: An opinion article expressing a newspaper's line; its plural is éditoriaux.

column6: Cette déclaration a déclenché une vive polémique.
column7: This statement triggered a fierce controversy.
column8: A lively, often aggressive public debate; one says « faire polémique » or « alimenter la polémique ».

column6: Elle a suivi un cursus universitaire très exigeant.
column7: She followed a very demanding university course.
column8: The whole programme of study leading to a degree; the final s is pronounced.

column6: La flânerie sur les quais de la Seine est un plaisir.
column7: Strolling along the quays of the Seine is a pleasure.
column8: Walking without a set aim, for pleasure; it is linked to the verb flâner.

column6: C'est la kermesse où tous les parents apportent un gâteau.
column7: It is the fair where all the parents bring a cake.
column8: An open-air popular fête, often organised for the benefit of a school or association.

column6: Elle a peint une aquarelle de la baie de Somme.
column7: She painted a watercolour of the Bay of Somme.
column8: Refers to the water-based painting technique or the painting made; a feminine noun in French.

column6: Les amis jouent à la pétanque sous les platanes.
column7: The friends play pétanque under the plane trees.
column8: A boules game very popular in the south of France; one plays « à la pétanque ».

column6: Son anxiété augmente avant chaque examen.
column7: Her anxiety increases before every exam.
column8: A word used both in everyday speech and clinically for intense worry; « crise d'angoisse » names an acute attack.

column6: Elle consulte un psychiatre pour sa dépression.
column7: She sees a psychiatrist for her depression.
column8: A mental illness; the word is also used in weather (« dépression atmosphérique ») and in economics.

column6: Cette addiction aux écrans inquiète beaucoup les parents.
column7: This screen addiction worries parents a great deal.
column8: A rather medical term; a close synonym is dépendance.

column6: Il attend une greffe de rein depuis longtemps.
column7: He has been waiting a long time for a kidney transplant.
column8: In the feminine, it means an organ transplant operation; le greffe (masculine) is a court office.

column6: Il a fait une rechute après quelques semaines de repos.
column7: He had a relapse after a few weeks of rest.
column8: Used for an illness that returns after an improvement; one says « faire une rechute ».

column6: Sa convalescence durera plusieurs semaines après l'opération.
column7: His recovery will last several weeks after the operation.
column8: The period of recovery following an illness or operation; the verb convalescer is rare.

column6: Cette insomnie chronique l'épuise depuis des mois.
column7: This chronic insomnia has been wearing her out for months.
column8: Difficulty sleeping; one says « souffrir d'insomnie » or « avoir des insomnies ».

column6: Ce handicap ne l'a jamais empêché de réussir.
column7: This disability never stopped him from succeeding.
column8: A common word; the phrase « personne en situation de handicap » is widely used in official language.

column6: La prévention reste le meilleur moyen de lutter contre les maladies.
column7: Prevention remains the best way to fight illness.
column8: A set of measures that avoid a risk; in public health one speaks of a « campagne de prévention ».

column6: Il souffre d'un épuisement total depuis plusieurs semaines.
column7: He has suffered total exhaustion for several weeks.
column8: Extreme tiredness; the expression « épuisement professionnel » corresponds to burn-out.

column6: Elle est en deuil depuis la mort de son père.
column7: She has been in mourning since her father's death.
column8: Refers to the loss of a loved one and the period of sorrow that follows; one says « faire son deuil ».

column6: Le patient est en rémission depuis deux ans.
column7: The patient has been in remission for two years.
column8: A medical term for the lasting easing of a disease, especially cancer; it does not always equal a cure.

column6: Elle a alimenté le débat avec des chiffres précis.
column7: She fueled the debate with precise figures.
column8: Transitive; figuratively it means to fuel, as in alimenter un débat.

column6: Nous avons contourné le centre-ville à cause des travaux.
column7: We bypassed the city centre because of the roadworks.
column8: Transitive: contourner un obstacle; also figurative, contourner une règle.

column6: Il a dissimulé la tache d'humidité derrière une armoire.
column7: He hid the damp stain behind a wardrobe.
column8: Transitive; it often implies a deliberate intention to keep something out of sight.

column6: Tu as esquivé toutes mes questions sur le budget.
column7: You dodged all my questions about the budget.
column8: Transitive: esquiver un coup, une question; it means to avoid skilfully.

column6: Ils ont persuadé le serveur de nous garder une table.
column7: They persuaded the waiter to keep a table for us.
column8: It is constructed persuader quelqu'un de faire quelque chose.

column6: Il a épuisé ses forces en escaladant la montagne.
column7: He exhausted his strength climbing the mountain.
column8: Transitive; used for strength and resources; the participle épuisé also means worn out.

column6: Nous avons réclamé un remboursement à l'agence de voyages.
column7: We demanded a refund from the travel agency.
column8: Direct transitive: réclamer quelque chose à quelqu'un; it implies a right, stronger than demander.

column6: Bien que le traitement ait aggravé ses douleurs, elle continue de marcher.
column7: Although the treatment has worsened her pain, she keeps walking.
column8: Transitive; the pronominal form s'aggraver means to get worse.

column6: Bien que la prime ait compensé la perte, il cherche un autre emploi.
column7: Although the bonus has offset the loss, he is looking for another job.
column8: Transitive: compenser une perte par quelque chose.

column6: Bien que la tempête ait déclenché une alerte, les vols restent maintenus.
column7: Although the storm has triggered an alert, the flights are still on.
column8: Transitive: déclencher une alerte, une crise, un conflit.

column6: Bien que le chef ait élaboré cette recette seul, il remercie son équipe.
column7: Although the chef devised this recipe alone, he thanks his team.
column8: Transitive; a fairly formal verb for working out a plan, a theory or a recipe.

column6: Bien qu'elle ait éliminé le sucre, elle se sent fatiguée.
column7: Although she has eliminated sugar, she feels tired.
column8: Transitive; in medicine and dietetics it also refers to getting rid of a substance.

column6: Bien que des grèves aient entravé la circulation, nous sommes arrivés à l'heure.
column7: Although strikes have hindered traffic, we arrived on time.
column8: Transitive; it means putting an obstacle in the way of a movement or an action.

column6: Bien que l'expert ait évalué ce meuble à mille euros, l'acheteur a hésité.
column7: Although the expert valued this piece of furniture at a thousand euros, the buyer hesitated.
column8: Transitive: évaluer un risque; one can say évaluer quelque chose à + a figure.

column6: Bien que le guide ait interpellé les touristes, personne n'a répondu.
column7: Although the guide has called out to the tourists, nobody answered.
column8: Transitive; it means to call out to someone loudly or to address them insistently.

column6: Bien que le film ait provoqué un scandale, il a fait salle comble.
column7: Although the film caused a scandal, it played to a full house.
column8: Transitive; it names the cause of an effect: provoquer un débat, une réaction.

column6: Bien que l'architecte ait harmonisé les couleurs, le salon paraît sombre.
column7: Although the architect has harmonized the colours, the living room looks dark.
column8: Transitive; the pronominal form s'harmoniser means to match.

column6: Si cet appareil amplifiait mieux le son, le concert serait parfait.
column7: If this device amplified the sound better, the concert would be perfect.
column8: Transitive; used for sounds and, figuratively, for problems or phenomena.

column6: Si nous anticipions les retards, nous réserverions un train plus tôt.
column7: If we anticipated the delays, we would book an earlier train.
column8: Transitive or intransitive; it means foreseeing something and acting in advance.

column6: Si le jury attribuait deux prix, les candidats seraient ravis.
column7: If the jury awarded two prizes, the candidates would be delighted.
column8: It is constructed attribuer quelque chose à quelqu'un.

column6: Si la direction bouleversait nos horaires, les équipes protesteraient.
column7: If management upended our schedules, the teams would protest.
column8: Transitive; it describes an upheaval that can be practical or emotional.

column6: Si le médecin cernait mieux les symptômes, le diagnostic serait plus rapide.
column7: If the doctor pinned down the symptoms better, the diagnosis would be faster.
column8: Transitive: cerner un problème means to delimit it in order to understand it.

column6: Si tu clarifiais ta demande, le vendeur te conseillerait mieux.
column7: If you clarified your request, the salesman would advise you better.
column8: Transitive: clarifier une situation, une position.

column6: Si nous comblions les fissures, la maison serait mieux isolée.
column7: If we filled the cracks, the house would be better insulated.
column8: Transitive: combler un vide, un retard; combler quelqu'un de cadeaux means to shower someone with gifts.

column6: Si le client contestait la facture, nous vérifierions chaque ligne.
column7: If the customer disputed the invoice, we would check every line.
column8: Transitive: contester une décision, une facture; it can also be used without an object.

column6: Si le chef dévoilait sa recette, tout le monde la copierait.
column7: If the chef unveiled his recipe, everyone would copy it.
column8: Transitive: dévoiler un secret, une statue, un projet.

column6: Si nous distinguions mieux ces deux tableaux, la visite serait passionnante.
column7: If we could distinguish these two paintings better, the visit would be fascinating.
column8: It is constructed distinguer A de B or distinguer A et B.

column6: Si vous aviez encouragé les enfants, ils auraient fini le match.
column7: If you had encouraged the children, they would have finished the match.
column8: It is constructed encourager quelqu'un à faire quelque chose; before o and a the g becomes ge (nous encourageons).

column6: Si l'hôtel avait exploité sa terrasse, il aurait attiré plus de clients.
column7: If the hotel had made use of its terrace, it would have attracted more guests.
column8: Transitive; it also has the negative sense of exploiting a person.

column6: En acclamant les musiciens, le public a prolongé la soirée.
column7: By cheering the musicians, the audience prolonged the evening.
column8: Transitive; it describes applause and shouts of approval.

column6: En argumentant calmement, elle a convaincu son patron.
column7: By arguing calmly, she convinced her boss.
column8: Often intransitive: argumenter en faveur de quelque chose.

column6: Ayant arbitré le match, il rentra épuisé.
column7: Having refereed the match, he went home exhausted.
column8: Transitive; used for matches and also for conflicts.

column6: En étayant son projet de chiffres, elle obtiendra le crédit.
column7: By backing up her project with figures, she will get the loan.
column8: Transitive; literally to prop up, figuratively to support with evidence.

column6: En façonnant l'argile, le potier crée un vase.
column7: By shaping the clay, the potter creates a vase.
column8: Transitive; it means giving form to a material or to a character.

column6: En freinant à la dernière seconde, le chauffeur a évité l'accident de justesse.
column7: By braking at the last second, the driver narrowly avoided the accident.
column8: Intransitive (freiner brusquement) or transitive (freiner l'inflation).

column6: En héritant de la ferme, ils ont changé de vie.
column7: By inheriting the farm, they changed their lives.
column8: It is usually constructed with de: hériter de quelque chose, hériter de quelqu'un.

column6: Ayant illustré le livre, elle partit en vacances.
column7: Having illustrated the book, she left on holiday.
column8: Transitive; used for pictures in a book and for examples that clarify an idea.

column6: En impliquant les habitants, la mairie a embelli le quartier.
column7: By involving the residents, the town hall made the neighbourhood nicer.
column8: Transitive; it means both to involve and to entail.

column6: En incarnant ce rôle, l'actrice a ému la salle.
column7: By playing this role, the actress moved the audience.
column8: Transitive; used for a theatre role or for an idea.

column6: En infligeant une amende, le contrôleur a surpris les voyageurs.
column7: By imposing a fine, the inspector surprised the passengers.
column8: Transitive: infliger une peine, une amende; before a and o the g becomes ge.

column6: En instaurant des pauses, l'entreprise a réduit le stress.
column7: By introducing breaks, the company reduced stress.
column8: Transitive; used for rules, regimes and habits.

column6: Le témoin avait invoqué la fatigue avant de quitter la salle.
column7: The witness had cited fatigue before leaving the room.
column8: Transitive: invoquer un motif, un argument, but also invoquer l'aide de quelqu'un.

column6: Nous avions modéré nos dépenses avant les vacances.
column7: We had moderated our spending before the holidays.
column8: Transitive; the accent changes in the present: je modère, nous modérons.

column6: Elle avait nuancé ses critiques avant la publication du roman.
column7: She had qualified her criticism before the novel was published.
column8: Transitive: nuancer ses propos; before a and o the c becomes ç (nous nuançons).

column6: Le cuisinier avait pallié le manque de crème avec du yaourt.
column7: The cook had made up for the lack of cream with yoghurt.
column8: Direct transitive: pallier un manque, un problème.

column6: Ce sucre est raffiné dans une usine près du port.
column7: This sugar is refined in a factory near the port.
column8: Transitive; literally to refine a substance, figuratively to make more subtle.

column6: Les manifestants ont été rassemblés par la police.
column7: The demonstrators were rounded up by the police.
column8: Transitive; the pronominal form se rassembler means to gather.

column6: Les passagers ont été privés de bagages pendant deux jours.
column7: The passengers were deprived of their luggage for two days.
column8: It is constructed priver quelqu'un de quelque chose.

column6: Cette méthode est prônée par de nombreux médecins.
column7: This method is advocated by many doctors.
column8: Transitive; it has a circumflex on the o.

column6: Le projet est piloté par une jeune ingénieure.
column7: The project is led by a young engineer.
column8: Transitive; it means piloting a vehicle or running a project.

column6: Il faut que vous accentuiez le contraste du tableau.
column7: You need to accentuate the contrast of the painting.
column8: Transitive; the pronominal form s'accentuer means to increase.

column6: Il faut que nous apaisions la douleur du patient.
column7: We must soothe the patient's pain.
column8: Transitive; used for pains, fears and conflicts.

column6: Il faut que le cuisinier éclaircisse la sauce.
column7: The cook needs to thin out the sauce.
column8: A regular -ir verb like finir (éclaircissons); it also means to clear up a mystery.

column6: Le médecin a expliqué que le virus affaiblissait les défenses.
column7: The doctor explained that the virus was weakening the defences.
column8: A regular -ir verb, conjugated like finir (affaiblissons).

column6: Le guide a précisé que la source jaillissait au printemps.
column7: The guide specified that the spring gushed in spring.
column8: A regular -ir verb (jaillissons); it describes a sudden spurt of liquid or light.

column6: Elle a répondu qu'elle ne fléchirait pas devant les pressions.
column7: She answered that she would not yield to pressure.
column8: A regular -ir verb; transitive (to bend) or intransitive (to give way).

column6: Ce cadeau ravirait ma grand-mère.
column7: This gift would delight my grandmother.
column8: A regular -ir verb (ravissons); past participle ravi.

column6: Les enfants se blottissent sous la couverture pendant l'orage.
column7: The children snuggle under the blanket during the storm.
column8: Almost always pronominal: se blottir; the passé composé uses être.

column6: Nous nous méfions des offres trop belles pour être vraies.
column7: We are wary of offers that seem too good to be true.
column8: Used only in the pronominal form: se méfier de quelqu'un or de quelque chose.

column6: Après la course, nous nous étirons longuement sur l'herbe.
column7: After the run, we stretch for a long time on the grass.
column8: Transitive; the pronominal form s'étirer means to stretch oneself.

column6: Elle se confie rarement à ses collègues.
column7: She rarely confides in her colleagues.
column8: Se confier à quelqu'un means to open up to someone; confier quelque chose à quelqu'un means to entrust.

column6: Ils se résignent à attendre le prochain train.
column7: They resign themselves to waiting for the next train.
column8: Used in the pronominal form: se résigner à + infinitive or noun.

column6: Personne ne peut contraindre un citoyen à voter contre sa conscience.
column7: Nobody can compel a citizen to vote against their conscience.
column8: Conjugated like craindre (contraignons); it takes contraindre quelqu'un à faire quelque chose.

column6: Ce règlement va astreindre les employés à un horaire strict.
column7: This rule will bind the employees to a strict schedule.
column8: Conjugated like craindre; it takes astreindre quelqu'un à quelque chose.

column6: On peut déduire ce chiffre du montant total de la facture.
column7: One can deduct this figure from the total amount of the invoice.
column8: Conjugated like conduire; past participle déduit; it also means to subtract a sum.

column6: Cette étiquette peut induire les clients en erreur.
column7: This label can mislead customers.
column8: Conjugated like conduire; the typical phrase is induire quelqu'un en erreur.

column6: Cette petite auberge va séduire tous les voyageurs.
column7: This little inn will charm all travellers.
column8: Conjugated like conduire; past participle séduit; it is also used for what attracts, not only for people.

column6: Le tabac peut nuire gravement à la santé.
column7: Tobacco can seriously harm your health.
column8: It takes à: nuire à quelqu'un; the past participle nui never agrees.

column6: Il faut accroître la production pour répondre à la demande.
column7: We must increase production to meet demand.
column8: Irregular; past participle accru; more formal than augmenter.

column6: Il suffit de dissoudre le sucre dans l'eau chaude.
column7: You just need to dissolve the sugar in hot water.
column8: Irregular; past participle dissous (feminine dissoute).

column6: Il faut extraire le miel de la ruche avec précaution.
column7: You have to extract the honey from the hive carefully.
column8: Conjugated like traire; past participle extrait.

column6: Personne ne doit soustraire ces documents au dossier médical.
column7: Nobody should remove these documents from the medical file.
column8: Conjugated like traire; soustraire quelque chose à quelqu'un or à quelque chose; it also means to subtract.

column6: Les locataires ne doivent pas enfreindre le règlement de l'immeuble.
column7: Tenants must not breach the building's rules.
column8: Conjugated like craindre; used with rules, laws and bans.

column6: La mairie veut restreindre la circulation dans le centre-ville.
column7: The town hall wants to restrict traffic in the city centre.
column8: Conjugated like craindre; past participle restreint.

column6: Le médecin va prescrire un traitement plus doux.
column7: The doctor is going to prescribe a gentler treatment.
column8: Conjugated like écrire; past participle prescrit; used for medicine and for rules.

column6: Un orage va interrompre le concert en plein air.
column7: A storm is going to interrupt the open-air concert.
column8: Conjugated like rompre; past participle interrompu.

column6: Certains cherchent à corrompre les arbitres du championnat.
column7: Some people try to bribe the referees of the championship.
column8: Conjugated like rompre; past participle corrompu; it means both to bribe and to corrupt.

column6: Nous voulons acquérir un appartement près du parc.
column7: We want to acquire a flat near the park.
column8: Irregular: j'acquiers, nous acquérons; past participle acquis; more formal than acheter.

column6: Il est difficile de contredire un expert reconnu.
column7: It is hard to contradict a recognised expert.
column8: Conjugated like dire, but the vous form is contredisez.

column6: Les habitants vont élire un nouveau maire dimanche.
column7: The residents will elect a new mayor on Sunday.
column8: Conjugated like lire; past participle élu.

column6: Cette publicité fallacieuse vante un fromage qui n'a rien d'artisanal.
column7: This misleading advert praises a cheese that is not at all artisanal.
column8: Feminine: fallacieuse. It describes arguments, promises or adverts that mislead.

column6: Les résultats de ce traitement ne sont pas assez probants.
column7: The results of this treatment are not conclusive enough.
column8: Feminine: probante. It is used for evidence, results or experiments that really prove something.

column6: Nous attendons des résultats tangibles avant d'investir davantage.
column7: We expect tangible results before investing any more.
column8: Same form in the feminine (une preuve tangible). It means touchable, and figuratively clearly visible, as with results.

column6: La fin ambiguë de ce roman divise encore les lecteurs.
column7: The ambiguous ending of this novel still divides readers.
column8: Feminine: ambiguë (with a diaeresis on the e). It describes words, situations or texts open to several readings.

column6: Un bonheur fugace nous a gagnés en haut de la colline.
column7: A fleeting happiness came over us at the top of the hill.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It is a fairly literary word for feelings, glances or memories that last very briefly.

column6: Le vieillissement est un phénomène inéluctable, mais on peut le ralentir.
column7: Ageing is an unavoidable phenomenon, but it can be slowed down.
column8: Same form in the feminine. A formal word for something that cannot be escaped.

column6: Ce vendeur propose un prix dérisoire pour un meuble ancien.
column7: This seller offers a derisory price for an antique piece of furniture.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes sums, prices or means so small they seem ridiculous.

column6: Le sucre caché dans les plats préparés exerce un effet insidieux.
column7: The sugar hidden in ready meals has an insidious effect.
column8: Feminine: insidieuse; the masculine plural stays insidieux. It describes a danger that works gradually and unnoticed.

column6: Le tourisme de masse a des effets pernicieux sur ce village.
column7: Mass tourism has harmful effects on this village.
column8: Feminine: pernicieuse; the masculine plural stays pernicieux. A formal word for something harmful, often slowly and discreetly.

column6: Votre dossier reste lacunaire : il manque deux justificatifs.
column7: Your file is still incomplete: two supporting documents are missing.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes a document, knowledge or account with missing parts.

column6: Cette bibliothèque propose un catalogue exhaustif des œuvres de Proust.
column7: This library offers an exhaustive catalogue of Proust's works.
column8: Feminine: exhaustive. It describes a list or study that leaves nothing out.

column6: Les effectifs pléthoriques de ce service ralentissent chaque décision.
column7: The excessive staff numbers in this department slow down every decision.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes something too numerous, such as staff, offers or documents.

column6: Le montage de cette armoire a été un travail laborieux.
column7: Assembling this wardrobe was laborious work.
column8: Feminine: laborieuse. It describes work that is long and tiring, or a result obtained with effort.

column6: Le silence du public après le concert fut éloquent.
column7: The silence of the audience after the concert was eloquent.
column8: Feminine: éloquente. It describes a person who speaks well and, figuratively, a gesture or fact that speaks for itself.

column6: Cette toux paraît anodine, mais elle dure depuis un mois.
column7: This cough seems harmless, but it has lasted for a month.
column8: Feminine: anodine. It describes something of little importance or seriousness, often with a hint of doubt.

column6: Ce grand magasin offre un choix inépuisable de chaussures.
column7: This department store offers an inexhaustible choice of shoes.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes resources, patience or topics that never run out.

column6: Notre rencontre fortuite dans un train pour Lyon a tout changé.
column7: Our chance meeting on a train to Lyon changed everything.
column8: Feminine: fortuite. A fairly formal word for an event due to chance, with no intention.

column6: Cette clause du contrat est devenue caduque l'an dernier.
column7: This contract clause lapsed last year.
column8: Feminine: caduque. In legal and administrative language it describes what is no longer valid.

column6: Ce menu cohérent associe des produits de saison.
column7: This coherent menu combines seasonal products.
column8: Feminine: cohérente. It describes a whole whose parts fit together logically.

column6: Le sourire équivoque de ce personnage intrigue les spectateurs.
column7: The equivocal smile of this character intrigues the audience.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It often carries a note of suspicion, more than ambigu; it also exists as a noun.

column6: Le guide jure que cette légende est véridique.
column7: The guide swears that this legend is true.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes an account or a person that tells the truth.

column6: Le problème d'humidité semble insoluble dans cet appartement.
column7: The damp problem seems unsolvable in this flat.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes a problem with no solution; in chemistry it also means not soluble.

column6: Ce marchand est un menteur notoire dans tout le quartier.
column7: This trader is a notorious liar throughout the neighbourhood.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes something known to everyone, often negative (un menteur notoire).

column6: Cette entreprise vise une croissance pérenne plutôt que rapide.
column7: This company aims for lasting growth rather than fast growth.
column8: Same form in the feminine. A formal word, common in business, for something that lasts over time.

column6: Un critique impartial doit juger le film sans préjugé.
column7: An impartial critic must judge the film without prejudice.
column8: Feminine: impartiale; masculine plural: impartiaux. It describes someone who judges without favouring anyone.

column6: Le point saillant de notre voyage fut la traversée du désert.
column7: The most striking point of our trip was crossing the desert.
column8: Feminine: saillante. It describes what stands out; it is often used with point or fait.

column6: La revente de vêtements d'occasion devient un commerce lucratif.
column7: Reselling second-hand clothes is becoming a lucrative business.
column8: Feminine: lucrative. It describes activities that earn money; in association à but non lucratif it means non-profit.

column6: Le chauffage de cet immeuble vétuste tombe souvent en panne.
column7: The heating in this run-down building often breaks down.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes buildings or equipment that are old and in poor condition.

column6: Nous avons suivi une route tortueuse jusqu'au village.
column7: We followed a winding road to the village.
column8: Feminine: tortueuse; the masculine plural stays tortueux. It describes roads and, figuratively, convoluted reasoning.

column6: Notre cabane de camping offrait un confort rudimentaire.
column7: Our camping hut offered only basic comfort.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes what is reduced to the essentials, sometimes insufficiently.

column6: Elle a choisi une robe sobre pour la cérémonie.
column7: She chose an understated dress for the ceremony.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes a style without excess; it also describes someone who drinks little.

column6: Les plats de ce buffet sont disparates mais délicieux.
column7: The dishes at this buffet are mismatched but delicious.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes elements very different from one another that do not form a coherent whole.

column6: Cette vénérable bibliothèque conserve des manuscrits du Moyen Âge.
column7: This venerable library keeps manuscripts from the Middle Ages.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It can come before the noun and shows respect for age or authority.

column6: La traversée du col fut périlleuse en plein hiver.
column7: Crossing the pass was perilous in the middle of winter.
column8: Feminine: périlleuse. A formal word for something full of danger or risk.

column6: Nous avons dormi dans un hébergement insolite, perché dans un arbre.
column7: We slept in an unusual place to stay, perched in a tree.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes what is out of the ordinary, with no negative judgement.

column6: Remplir ces formulaires est une tâche fastidieuse.
column7: Filling in these forms is a tedious task.
column8: Feminine: fastidieuse. It means boring and repetitive, not annoying in the Italian sense of fastidioso.

column6: Le service de ce restaurant est irréprochable.
column7: The service at this restaurant is impeccable.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes behaviour or work with nothing to criticise.

column6: Prendre ce médicament sans ordonnance serait hasardeux.
column7: Taking this medicine without a prescription would be risky.
column8: It starts with an aspirated «h»: no liaison or elision.

column6: Ce n'est pas le moment opportun pour demander une augmentation.
column7: This is not the right moment to ask for a raise.
column8: Feminine: opportune. It describes what comes at the right time or suits the situation.

column6: Le message implicite de ce film critique la société moderne.
column7: The implicit message of this film criticises modern society.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes what is not said openly but understood; the opposite of explicite.

column6: Les conditions de la garantie doivent être explicites.
column7: The terms of the warranty must be explicit.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes what is stated clearly and precisely; the opposite of implicite.

column6: Il a passé la soirée à des discussions futiles.
column7: He spent the evening in trivial discussions.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes what has little importance or value.

column6: Cette douleur tenace l'empêche de dormir.
column7: This persistent pain keeps him from sleeping.
column8: Same form in the feminine. It describes pain, smells or prejudices that are hard to get rid of; of a person, it means someone who does not give up.

column6: Ils ont préparé un somptueux repas de fête.
column7: They prepared a sumptuous festive meal.
column8: Feminine: somptueuse; the masculine plural stays somptueux. It can come before or after the noun.

column5: not at all, by no means
column6: Je ne suis nullement inquiet pour le résultat de l'examen.
column7: I am not at all worried about the result of the exam.
column8: A strong negation used with ne before the verb. A formal word, more emphatic than pas du tout.

column6: La vendeuse a d'emblée proposé une réduction.
column7: The saleswoman offered a discount right away.
column8: The word contains an apostrophe (d'emblée). It means doing something from the very first moment, without hesitation.

column6: La caution sera remboursée intégralement si l'appartement est propre.
column7: The deposit will be refunded in full if the flat is clean.
column8: It comes from the adjective intégral. It is used with verbs like payer, rembourser, lire to mean leaving nothing out.

column5: later on, at a later date
column6: Nous vous communiquerons les horaires du voyage ultérieurement.
column7: We will give you the travel times at a later date.
column8: Administrative and formal: it refers to an unspecified later moment.

column6: L'artiste avait antérieurement exposé dans plusieurs galeries parisiennes.
column7: The artist had previously exhibited in several Paris galleries.
column8: Formal; the opposite of ultérieurement. It is often found as antérieurement à + noun.

column6: Un plat savoureux n'est pas nécessairement compliqué.
column7: A tasty dish is not necessarily complicated.
column8: Very common in the negative form pas nécessairement, meaning not always.

column6: Autrefois, ce boulanger travaillait exclusivement avec de la farine locale.
column7: In the past, this baker worked exclusively with local flour.
column8: Stronger and more formal than seulement: it excludes every other possibility.

column6: L'équipe s'est résolument engagée dans ce projet.
column7: The team has committed itself resolutely to this project.
column8: It shows determination without hesitation; it goes with verbs like s'engager, refuser, se tourner vers.

column6: Comment organiserez-vous concrètement ce voyage ?
column7: How will you organise this trip in practice?
column8: Often used at the start of a sentence to ask for or give practical details.

column6: Il a sciemment caché les défauts de la voiture.
column7: He knowingly hid the car's faults.
column8: It is spelled with -emment but pronounced [amɑ̃]. A formal word, typical of legal language.

column6: Il a délibérément ignoré les conseils de son médecin.
column7: He deliberately ignored his doctor's advice.
column8: It stresses that the action is willed and conscious; a more common synonym of sciemment.

column6: Le jury a unanimement salué ce documentaire.
column7: The jury unanimously praised this documentary.
column8: It comes from unanime. It is used with verbs like saluer, approuver, reconnaître, condamner.

column6: Elle souhaitait ardemment retrouver sa maison d'enfance.
column7: She ardently wished to find her childhood home again.
column8: It comes from ardent and is pronounced [aʁdamɑ̃]. A formal word, used with souhaiter, désirer, espérer.

column6: Vous pourriez garder la chambre jusqu'à midi moyennant un supplément.
column7: You could keep the room until noon for an extra charge.
column8: A formal word that introduces a payment or condition that makes something possible.

column5: with, from, at (a person or office)
column6: Nous nous renseignerons auprès de l'office de tourisme.
column7: We will ask at the tourist office.
column8: It is always followed by de (auprès de) before a person or institution, as in se renseigner auprès de.

column6: On devrait prendre soin de soi pour rester en bonne santé.
column7: One should look after oneself to stay in good health.
column8: A stressed reflexive pronoun referring to an indefinite or generic subject (on, chacun, il faut). With je or tu use moi or toi.

column6: Il est important de respecter autrui.
column7: It is important to respect others.
column8: Used only in the singular and almost always as an object; formal register.

column6: Tel est le cas pour beaucoup de jeunes.
column7: Such is the case for many young people.
column8: It is an adjective: «tel que», «tel quel»; feminine «telle», plurals «tels» and «telles».

column6: Nul n'est censé ignorer la loi.
column7: No one is supposed to ignore the law.
column8: As a pronoun it is formal and goes with ne; as an adjective nul means null.

column5: to lead to, to result in
column6: Ces négociations ont abouti à un accord.
column7: These negotiations led to an agreement.
column8: It takes «à»: «aboutir à» + noun or infinitive.

column6: Ce projet suscite beaucoup d'intérêt.
column7: This project arouses a lot of interest.
column8: It is used with abstract nouns: «susciter l'intérêt, la curiosité, la polémique».

column6: Nous entamons les négociations demain.
column7: We start the negotiations tomorrow.
column8: It is used for long or delicate processes; it also means to make a first cut in something.

column6: Nous décelons une erreur dans ce rapport.
column7: We detect an error in this report.
column8: In the present some forms take a grave accent: «je décèle».

column6: Les experts préconisent une réforme rapide.
column7: Experts advocate a quick reform.
column8: It is more formal than «conseiller»; used for measures and methods.

column6: Nous remédions à ce problème rapidement.
column7: We are quickly remedying this problem.
column8: It always takes «à»: «remédier à quelque chose».

column6: Le maire déplore ce manque de moyens.
column7: The mayor deplores this lack of resources.
column8: It is stronger and more formal than «regretter».

column6: Le bilan de l'année est très positif.
column7: The year's assessment is very positive.
column8: It means both a financial balance sheet and an overall assessment: «faire le bilan».

column6: L'essor du tourisme change la région.
column7: The boom in tourism is changing the region.
column8: It is used almost only in the singular: «prendre son essor».

column6: Ce clivage divise la société depuis longtemps.
column7: This divide has split society for a long time.
column8: It is used for social or political divisions.

column6: L'éducation est un levier de changement.
column7: Education is a lever for change.
column8: It is also used figuratively: «un levier d'action».

column6: L'écart entre les prix augmente chaque mois.
column7: The gap between prices grows every month.
column8: It is also used in «à l'écart» (aside).

column6: Cette habitude est néfaste pour la santé.
column7: This habit is harmful to health.
column8: It has the same form for masculine and feminine; it is more formal than «mauvais».

column6: Cette situation est inédite en Europe.
column7: This situation is unprecedented in Europe.
column8: It means both «never seen before» and «unpublished».

column6: Dorénavant, nous travaillerons à distance.
column7: From now on, we will work remotely.
column8: It is more formal than «désormais» and usually introduces a new rule.

column6: Leur périple à travers l'Asie a duré six mois.
column7: Their trip across Asia lasted six months.
column8: Denotes a long journey with many stages, often adventurous. It is more literary than voyage.

column6: Nous avons réservé un gîte près de la rivière.
column7: We booked a holiday cottage near the river.
column8: In France it is a rented rural lodging, usually with a kitchen. It is not a hotel.

column6: La cueillette des fraises commence dès le mois de mai.
column7: Strawberry picking starts as early as May.
column8: It refers to picking fruit, berries or mushrooms by hand, often as a leisure activity.

column6: Elle a trouvé cette lampe ancienne dans une brocante.
column7: She found this old lamp at a flea market.
column8: It means both the trade in second-hand goods and the market or shop where they are sold.

column6: Nous irons au vernissage de l'exposition samedi soir.
column7: We will go to the exhibition opening on Saturday evening.
column8: It is the opening evening of an art exhibition, usually by invitation.

column6: Chaque courbature me rappelait la longue marche d'hier.
column7: Every muscle ache reminded me of yesterday's long walk.
column8: It is often used in the plural: avoir des courbatures means to be sore after exertion.

column6: Le soir, elle boit une tisane au tilleul.
column7: In the evening, she drinks a linden herbal tea.
column8: It means an infusion of herbs or flowers, usually without tea and without caffeine.

column6: La fanfare du village a ouvert le défilé.
column7: The village brass band opened the parade.
column8: It means a band of brass and percussion, and also the piece played by trumpets.

column6: Les touristes déambulent dans les ruelles de la vieille ville.
column7: The tourists stroll through the alleys of the old town.
column8: A regular -er verb meaning to walk without a goal and without hurry.

column6: Elle passe ses dimanches en flânant au bord de la Seine.
column7: She spends her Sundays strolling along the Seine.
column8: It means to walk unhurriedly, enjoying the atmosphere of a city.

column6: Il grignote des biscuits devant la télé toute la soirée.
column7: He nibbles biscuits in front of the TV all evening.
column8: It means to eat a little and often between meals. It can be intransitive or take an object.

column6: Ils sillonnent la Bretagne en camping-car chaque été.
column7: They crisscross Brittany by camper van every summer.
column8: It is a direct transitive verb meaning to travel across a region in every direction.

column6: Elle postule à un poste de chef de projet.
column7: She is applying for a project manager position.
column8: It is usually followed by à or pour: postuler à un poste.

column6: Mon voisin jeûne chaque année pendant le ramadan.
column7: My neighbour fasts every year during Ramadan.
column8: It is intransitive: to go without food for a time, for medical or religious reasons.

column6: Nous aérons la chambre tous les matins.
column7: We air the bedroom every morning.
column8: It is used for airing a room. The accent changes before silent endings: j'aère.

column6: Nous avons dormi dans un village pittoresque au bord de la mer.
column7: We slept in a picturesque village by the sea.
column8: It has the same form in the feminine: une rue pittoresque.

column6: Le métro était bondé à cause de la grève.
column7: The metro was packed because of the strike.
column8: It agrees in gender and number: bondée, bondés, bondées. It describes places or vehicles full of people.

column6: Ce pain croustillant sort tout juste du four.
column7: This crispy bread has just come out of the oven.
column8: The feminine is croustillante. It describes bread, skin or fried chicken.

column6: Cette application propose une façon ludique d'apprendre.
column7: This app offers a playful way of learning.
column8: It has the same form in the feminine. It relates to play or is fun like a game.

column6: L'entretien de cette vieille maison reste très onéreux.
column7: Maintaining this old house remains very costly.
column8: It is formal and appears in administrative and journalistic texts. The feminine is onéreuse.

column6: Jadis, ce quartier était un village de pêcheurs.
column7: Long ago, this district was a fishing village.
column8: A literary adverb that points to a distant past.

column6: Il n'y a guère de monde sur la plage en hiver.
column7: There is hardly anyone on the beach in winter.
column8: It is used with ne: ne ... guère means hardly, not much. The register is rather formal.

column6: Ce retard ne m'a aucunement dérangé pendant le voyage.
column7: This delay did not bother me at all during the trip.
column8: It is used with ne and strengthens the negation. The register is formal.

column6: Le directeur était précédemment responsable d'une usine voisine.
column7: The director was previously in charge of a nearby factory.
column8: A formal adverb meaning earlier, at a previous time. It is typical of written texts.

column6: Vu le prix, ce billet est vraiment trop cher.
column7: Given the price, this ticket is really too expensive.
column8: As a preposition it is invariable and comes before a noun: vu la situation.

column6: Sitôt arrivés à l'hôtel, nous avons défait les valises.
column7: As soon as we arrived at the hotel, we unpacked the suitcases.
column8: Literary or formal register. It takes a past participle or the form sitôt que.
